title: The Circleville Poison Pen Letters Mystery
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the Circleville Poison Pen Letters case in Circleville, Ohio: a campaign of threatening letters, signs and postcards over nearly twenty years targeting Mary Gillespie, her husband Ron's death in a drunk-driving crash, the booby-trapped sign that led to Paul Freshour's attempted murder conviction, and the competing theories about who the letter writer was. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about the Flannan Isles lighthouse mystery.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Circleville case as a true crime mystery without murder, note its Unsolved Mysteries exposure, and list their sources.

segments.title: First letters and the Gillespie family
segments.summary: Mary Gillespie, a school bus driver in Circleville, receives a threatening letter accusing her of an affair with superintendent Gordon Massey. Letters follow her husband Ron, and the couple brings in relatives Karen and Paul Freshour.

segments.title: Ron Gillespie's death
segments.summary: Paul Freshour sends a threatening letter to David Longberry, and the letters briefly stop before signs appear. Ron Gillespie dies in a single-vehicle crash near home after a phone call with the letter writer; he had a blood alcohol level of 0.16, a missing round from his gun, and the sheriff's handling was questioned.

segments.title: Aftermath, divorce and Mary's affair
segments.summary: Paul and Karen Freshour divorce and Karen moves onto Mary's property. Mary later admits an affair with Massey, which the hosts discuss in context of other accusations against the superintendent.

segments.title: Expansion of letters and the booby-trapped sign
segments.summary: The letters spread to businesses and townspeople in the 1980s. In February 1983 Mary finds a booby-trapped sign threatening her daughter; it contains a .25 caliber handgun that police trace to a gun Paul Freshour had bought secondhand.

segments.title: Paul Freshour's arrest and trial
segments.summary: Sheriff Radcliff arrests Paul Freshour after an improvised handwriting test and Karen's statement about letters found in the house. At trial in 1983 the letters are admitted, a handwriting analyst testifies, and Paul is convicted and sentenced to seven to twenty-five years. Paul denies involvement, saying the gun was stolen.

segments.title: Prison, parole and the letters continuing
segments.summary: Letters keep arriving while Paul is in prison, which is used against him at parole hearings. He is released after about eleven years and sets up a website professing innocence. The hosts discuss the lack of a clear motive.

segments.title: Scope of the letter campaign and other targets
segments.summary: More than a thousand letters, postcards and signs over almost two decades targeted many townspeople, including a doctor with a past, the prosecutor Roger Klein, and the coroner. Some accusations were true. Mark Freshour's 2002 death and the Massey son William are mentioned as possible suspects.

segments.title: Theories about the letter writer
segments.summary: The hosts weigh suspects: Karen Freshour (per Martin Yant's theory), David Longberry, Gordon Massey, and Paul Freshour himself, citing handwriting analysis, fingerprints and the letters stopping after his release. Each host states a favored theory.

segments.title: Listener mail: Flannan Isles
segments.summary: Hosts read listener Allison from Toronto's proposed explanation for the Flannan Isles lighthouse disappearance: a rogue wave swept away the three keepers.
